historical_reviews.deepseek: The generic Pxe selector does not establish which NIC, VLAN, DHCP offer or boot file was used, and it omits BIOS prerequisites, console proof, clear timing and recovery.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly requires an exact network boot chain and no-install boundary rather than treating bootparam as proof of PXE success.
historical_reviews.history: No earlier exact source identity record exists.
historical_reviews.v3_1: PXE is a distributed boot transaction. Acceptance must correlate the node's intended NIC/MAC with DHCP lease, next-server, boot filename and the pre-OS artifact marker. A BMC override can be correct while a rogue or wrong-scope PXE service supplies an unsafe image.

original_test_intent: Validate a one-time EFI PXE override on the approved node, prove it reaches the intended isolated PXE service and artifact without installation, then consume the flag and restore the normal boot path.
original_method: Verify BIOS network prerequisites and exact NIC/MAC/VLAN, capture BootOrder and network baseline, validate the approved DHCP/next-server/boot-file artifact, set and read the protected one-time PXE override, reboot with approval, correlate server and console evidence to the safe marker, then confirm auto-clear, unchanged order and normal health.
manual_activity: The owner approves the PXE fixture and artifact; an operator observes POST/console, prevents installer writes, controls recovery and owns the verdict.
required_inputs: PXE NIC, MAC, VLAN and link mapping
DHCP scope, next-server and boot-file mapping
Approved signed/hashed artifact and safe marker
Maintenance window, console/PDU recovery and protected credentials
safety_requirements: Use an isolated approved PXE service
Never accept generic reachability as artifact proof
Stop on wrong NIC, VLAN, offer, image, installer, loop or timeout
Preserve logs and PXE server evidence
Clear override, restore normal boot and never auto-retry
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, NIC and PXE chain
Collect DHCP, PXE, POST and console timeline
Verify exact artifact marker and no write
Check flag consumption, order and health
engineer_actions: Observe console and stop unsafe flow

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: A Once/Pxe PATCH is relevant but insufficient: it guesses the network target, exposes credentials, bypasses TLS and omits the four BIOS checks, DHCP/artifact proof and cleanup.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported protected one-time PXE control only after binding the exact NIC/MAC/VLAN and isolated service; verify the signed artifact through server plus console evidence and restore boot state.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The 10/30-minute estimates, BIOS checks, reboot and 60-second +/-10% note remain subject to vendor confirmation; no log clearing or install is added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a single transaction ledger linking target identity, NIC/MAC/VLAN, DHCP offer, next-server, boot filename/hash, console marker, flag consumption and unchanged BootOrder.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds network-path and artifact identity plus a hard no-install boundary and deterministic recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Override readback alone cannot prove which interface or server supplied the executed image.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Competing DHCP services or firmware NIC ordering can redirect the boot; isolation and exact server logs are essential.

project_override_considerations: The Project must define the intended PXE artifact and safe stopping point. Any installer execution or BIOS setting mutation requires separate authorization and recovery.
expected_evidence: Approved target, BIOS prerequisites, NIC/MAC/VLAN and normal boot baseline
PXE service, DHCP, boot-file and artifact identity evidence
Protected one-time override and bootparam readback
Consumed flag, unchanged BootOrder, restored OS/BMC/network health
Preserved logs, recovery and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure, Criteria and DeepSeek consistently target one-time PXE boot. Missing fixture identity and artifact detail are required inputs, not conflicting Master branches.

blocked_analysis.analysis: PXE fixture, exact mapping, artifact, console and recovery are normal prerequisites; execution blocks only if they cannot be established safely.

review_improvement: Replaces generic PXE reachability with an identity-linked network boot transaction and explicit no-install, clear and recovery checks.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PXE boot is only trustworthy when the BMC target, physical NIC, DHCP lease, boot server and executed artifact form a closed chain. Without that chain, a successful pre-OS screen could come from the wrong VLAN or an unauthorized installer. Server-side request logs and a unique console marker jointly establish the intended path while flag and BootOrder checks prevent latent boot disruption.
